body:
sanjay: Quick follow-up to the on-prem packaging RFC — I dug into interrupted transfers and have a concrete proposal for resume+compact semantics for nodes that only get partial artifact sets. TL;DR: make installs idempotent by switching to segmented checkpoints and a small fast-path compaction that can run offline.

maria: sketch it out please — worried about edge cases where a node has a newer manifest but missing segments.

sanjay: Yes. Proposal in bullets: 
- split bundles into ordered segments S0..SN with independent checksums.
- include a lightweight segment-index.json in the seed image with per-segment CID & size.
- agents maintain a local segment state: present/missing/corrupt. Resume tries segment-level fetches only.
- activation requires a two-phase apply: verify segments -> assemble staging area -> atomic swap.
- compaction: if node has >80% segments present but limited disk, run a compacter that merges small leftovers into a single verified segment before activation.

alex: re: compaction — how do we avoid OOM when merging big segments on low-disk nodes?

sanjay: compactor must stream-merge with limited memory buffer and write out a new segment file to the staging mount (not root). If staging unavailable, fallback to skip compaction and require full download or fallback variant.

jen: what about signature/attestation? we need to ensure compacted segment is still verifiable by the verifier.

sanjay: good point. Approach: compaction produces a new segment with a deterministic header that includes the original segment CIDs list. We then have two options:
1) compacter signs the new segment with an agent-local ephemeral key and uploads the proof to the control-plane to be notarized (requires connectivity), OR
2) verifier supports a "composite" proof: client sends original CIDs + compaction manifest and verifier replays digest chain to confirm equivalence. Option 2 is offline-friendly but slightly heavier.

maria: I like option 2 for air-gapped installs. fewer outbound dependencies. But add a per-node compaction-policy to avoid drift between clusters.

ops-bot: reminder: new rollout window for on-prem v0.9.3 is scheduled 2026-10-02 23:00 UTC. :bell:

paul: operational question — how do we record partial-sync state so that after a powercycle the agent doesn't re-download already present segments?

sanjay: store a small sqlite in /var/lib/redwood-agent/segments.db with segment id, size, checksum, last-verified-ts. DB is written atomically. On startup agent reparses DB and runs a quick verify on present files (checksum). If mismatch, mark corrupt and requeue.

irene: can we keep the DB format pluggable? some customers want audit-only append-only logs.

sanjay: yes — design will expose an interface: SegmentStore { list(), mark_present(), mark_corrupt(), compact(), snapshot() }. Default is sqlite, we ship a simple append-audit mode too.

alex: failure modes — what if compaction runs concurrently with resume and both touch staging? Race conditions.

sanjay: compaction takes a lock on the staging path. Resume will try to acquire same lock, if blocked it waits with exponential backoff. We also expose a "dry-run" verify so resume can confirm integrity without mutating files.

jen: testing matrix? I want to see: interrupted download, corrupt segment, compaction on limited disk, offline verifier using composite proofs, node reboot mid-apply.

sanjay: will draft a test plan and add to the RFC follow-up. Quick checklist I will add to PR: 
- unit tests for segment index parsing
- e2e with synthetic slow link (tc/netem) 
- compaction integration test on 2GB disk VM
- verifier acceptance tests for composite proof replay

maria: one more: dataset/model artifacts may have internal symlinks. Verify assembler preserves symlink semantics in compaction.

sanjay: noted. assembler must preserve metadata (mode, uid/gid, symlinks) and store them in the compaction header.

paul: ops concern — we should expose metrics: segments_total, segments_present, segment_compactions, last_compaction_duration.

sanjay: yes. will add Prometheus metrics and a debug endpoint /internal/segments/status returning index + state. It will be secured behind node auth.

maria: ok great. please post the RFC patch when ready. this seems non-overlapping with previous manifest-first proposals.

sanjay: will do. I'll include a short implementation timeline: prototype (2w), integration tests (1w), canary in Dedicated (1w), ship opt-in (2w).

alex: :thumbsup:

jen: thanks, this addresses a lot of customer pain.

sanjay: Thanks all — I'll open the PR with design doc + tests by EOD tomorrow.
